issues.title: How big can an URI template be?
issues.author: aretana
issues.body:
> Question: how big can an URI template be?

I don't believe URI or URI templates specification define a ceiling.
Clearly, to reliably fit URI template into BGP UPDATE message it must be constrained to a reasonable length. How would you recommend defining it?

_Originally posted by @yaroslavros in https://github.com/yaroslavros/bgp-masque-tunnel/issues/1#issuecomment-4740186341_

comments.author: aretana
comments.body:
We need to check the bounds and add some text about the size of the BGP UPDATE message and the potential need to use extended messages.

This may be a good topic for Operational Considerations: if the template is too large, the tunnel won't be usable.

pulls.title: Initial review
pulls.author: aretana
pulls.body:
I took an initial look at the draft and made some changes:

- instead of indicating which sub-TLVs are not applicable, I changed the logic to list the ones that are (this should be easier to maintain)
- added some minor things to be compliant with what idr expects (https://wiki.ietf.org/group/idr/TEA-templates)
- added some validation text

I think we could publish this initial version, but I do want to go back for a deeper look into some things:

- look in detail at the allowed Sub-TLVs
- I didn't look into the URI Template or ALPN sub-TLVs
- The Operational and Security Considerations look good, but I want to think about them a little more

comments.author: yaroslavros
comments.body: @aretana please review the update text

4k is the maximum size of a BGP UPDATE, so the guidance would have to be much lower than that to account for the other variable information in the update.

The last paragraph already mentioned 1k, which is 10x the size you said is rarely exceeded.  Instead of a value here, we should indicate what should be taken into account if the template size could cause the update to exceed the max size: i.e., use extended messages.

If you agree with the approach, I can suggest text.

Similar comment here about mentioning a specific size.

But it seems important to instead RECOMMEND not carrying large proxy configuration objects.
`SHOULD ignore the MASQUE Tunnel Encapsulation TLV`

I think concrete guidance would still be beneficial for proxy implementors who don't know much about BGP.

I agree that the 4096 should not be mentioned at all, <del>640kb</del> 1024 is long enough for all the reasonable use cases.

Please suggest edit!

I did, but I don't know if I screwed up the format. :-(

The intent is for the paragraphs starting with "Senders should keep..." to read:

> Senders should keep URI Template Values as short as practical. In deployments
> where BGP Extended Messages are not expected to be fully supported, URI Template
> Values should be kept small enough that the complete BGP UPDATE message,
> including all path attributes, NLRI, and protocol overhead, can be carried
> without requiring BGP Extended Messages. 
> 
> As a practical guideline, URI Template Values intended for such deployments
> SHOULD NOT exceed 1024 octets. This limit is intended to avoid using BGP to
> carry large proxy configuration objects. Implementations MAY apply a smaller
> configurable local limit. If the URI Template Value exceeds the receiver's
> supported or configured limit, the receiver SHOULD ignore the enclosing MASQUE
> Tunnel Encapsulation TLV.
> 
> If the length of the URI Template results in the BGP UPDATE exceeding the
> maximum message size, the result may include a lack of reachability, as detailed
> in [RFC8654]. If BGP Extended Messages are partially supported, the BGP Tunnel
> Encapsulation Attribute may be discarded [RFC8654], as it is eligible under the
> "attribute discard" approach of [RFC7606], which would result in the information
> not reaching the intended receivers.
